Hi Alex — thanks, good questions. Below is language you can place in the questionnaire, followed by operational details and exceptions.

Official statement (short):
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided prompts, generated outputs, embeddings, or customer metadata to train or improve our public or internal models. Data submitted to Redwood for inference is processed to serve the request and is not included in model training datasets, except where explicit written consent has been obtained for a named program."

Operational retention summary (defaults, unless otherwise contracted):
- Request/response payloads (transit & processing logs): retained 30 days by default in live processing logs.
- Structured request metadata (headers, timestamps, basic routing): retained 90 days for billing and analytics by default.
- Debug snapshots & escalations: ephemeral debug snapshots are retained up to 14 days by default and are only captured if the customer enables verbose debugging or if an incident requires deeper inspection. For escalations, a snapshot may be preserved longer (90 days) but only with customer notification and approval when necessary.
- Backups & snapshots: encrypted nightly backups are retained for 45 days in rolling backups; long-term archival copies (used for legal/compliance holds) are stored beyond that only under specific custodial processes and with limited access.
- KV cache: in-memory per-session caches are ephemeral and are not persisted to long-term storage; we do not use KV contents for training.

Deletion and purge process:
- Soft-delete (tombstone): when a customer requests deletion, items are tombstoned immediately and are made inaccessible from the product and APIs within 24 hours.
- Hard purge: background processes permanently delete tombstoned items from primary stores within 30–45 days depending on shard compaction windows.
- Backups: backup files that may have contained the data are rotated and expire according to the backup retention window (45 days default) and are not reconstituted for model training. Long-term archival removal requires a manual eviction step and is completed within 90 days for most customers; we can accelerate if contractually required.

Exceptions and safeguards:
- Aggregated telemetry used for platform improvements is anonymized and sampled. This telemetry does not contain raw customer prompts or outputs; customers may opt out of telemetry collection.
- Any request to use customer data for model improvement requires an explicit, documented agreement and a separate opt-in process.

Attachments: redwood_no_training_attestation.pdf (signed attestation), data_retention_matrix_v3.xlsx (detailed retention matrix).

I'll attach the signed attestation and the retention matrix PDF to this thread. If you need a DocuSign or formal letter on company letterhead for procurement, we can generate that quickly.

Thanks,
Mina

Alex — brief answers to the follow-ups:
- Accelerated purge: yes. For customer-specific accelerated purges we offer an expedited purge process (contract or paid service). SLA: we commit to making data inaccessible in product within 24 hours and completing hard purge across primary stores within 7 business days; backup eviction and archival removal target 30 days but can be accelerated with an explicit contractual clause.
- Audit trail: we maintain immutable deletion audit logs (write-once entries) recording the delete request, tombstone timestamp, and hard purge completion. We can provide a deletion report for regulators showing those timestamps and operator IDs.
- Separation of artifacts: debug snapshots and escalation artifacts are strictly access-controlled. They are only accessible to on-call engineers or support staff during incident resolution and are not used in any model training pipeline. Any internal use of customer artifacts for platform-level engineering is anonymized and reviewed by compliance; product or model engineering teams never ingest raw customer prompts for training without explicit opt-in.

Next steps: attaching the signed attestation and the retention matrix PDF now. If procurement wants a letter on letterhead or DocuSign, I can have legal prepare it and send it to the procurement contact you mentioned.

Best,
Naomi
